overall_reason: The copy is concrete and belongs to the trade (movements, withdrawal dates, holding numbers, inspectors, £12 a month per farm), but it sits on the stock SaaS skeleton: device-mock hero, three equal tile-icon cards, product table with check list, 1-2-3 steps band, pricing plus FAQ, closing CTA band.

findings.where: whole page, image.png top to bottom
findings.evidence: Failed T-STOCK-ORDER: sections in order are (1) hero with phone product mock [stock], (2) 'Three records, one place.' three equal cards [stock], (3) 'Ready when they knock.' copy + table mock, (4) 'Set up before tea.' 1-2-3 steps on a green band [stock], (5) £12 pricing card beside an FAQ [stock FAQ], (6) 'Put the book in your pocket.' closing CTA band [stock], (7) footer. Five stock sections in the stock order caps the read at mixed. T-MIRROR: a neighbouring brief (a dairy compliance app, a vet-records app) would get the same sequence.
findings.before: hero mock / 3 cards / feature+mock / 1-2-3 / pricing+FAQ / CTA band
findings.after: Change one structural decision and name it: e.g. let the inspection report (the medicine record) be the page's spine, scrolling through one real day of entries, and fold the three cards and the steps into it
findings.why: Specific words on a default skeleton still read as a default page.

findings.evidence: Three equal-width cards with the same radius, border and fill, each: letter tile (MV / RX / FW) above a serif heading, one-sentence sub-line, then three dashed-rule bullet rows. The tiles do earn something (they match the entry codes in the phone mock), but the container recipe is the card kit.
findings.before: 3 x [tile, h3, sub, 3 bullets] in identical cards
findings.after: Keep the MV/RX/FW codes but drop the boxes: set the three records as a table or a ruled list with the code in the margin, matching how the app itself shows entries
findings.why: Equal boxed cards are the default container; the content here is a list of record types and reads better as one.

findings.where: hero right: phone mock 'Hill Farm log' (x880-1190, y140-585)
findings.evidence: A drawn phone with a thick rounded bezel and soft drop shadow frames HTML-styled list rows; this is a built device mock, not a capture of the app (image-only: cannot confirm whether the product exists). The rows themselves are good sample data ('Wormer, batch 4471 / 8 lambs, 21 day withdrawal').
findings.before: CSS phone bezel around styled rows
findings.after: Use a real screenshot of the app in that state (IMG-116), shown without a drawn bezel; if the product is not built, keep the rows but label the panel as a design (IMG-121)
findings.why: Drawn device chrome is a template prop; the rows carry the meaning.

findings.evidence: T-RIVAL-NAME: swap in another livestock-records app and 'Farm records, done in the yard.', 'Three records, one place.' and 'Ready when they knock.' all stay true; what only Fieldbook can say (flat £12 per farm, 'Works without signal', 'Stock left in the cabinet') sits in sub-lines and bullets, not headings. Heads are category-specific, not business-specific; concept is not capped because the price and offline claims are concrete.
findings.after: Promote a differentiator into a heading, e.g. 'One price per farm, every worker's phone' (from the pricing card)
findings.why: Headings are what a skimmer reads; the specific facts should be there.

findings.where: nav, hero, pricing card, closing band
findings.evidence: One action in four wordings: 'Start free trial' (nav, closing band), 'Try it free for 30 days' (hero), 'Start your 30 day trial' (pricing). The price and trial ('£12 a month per farm', 'Thirty days free, then £12 a month per farm') are stated three times.
findings.before: "Try it free for 30 days" / "Start your 30 day trial" / "Start free trial"
findings.after: One label everywhere, e.g. 'Start 30-day trial'; state the price once in the hero and once in pricing, and cut the closing band's restatement
findings.why: Variant labels for one action are template drift; repetition stands in for content.

findings.where: 'Ready when they knock.' sub-line; FAQ last answer
findings.evidence: T-THREE-LINE: 'Pull any period into a clean report in seconds.' (not falsifiable: which report, how long) and 'Most farms do just that.' (unsourced generalisation). T-FRESH-READER generic lines: those two and 'Put the book in your pocket.'
findings.before: "Pull any period into a clean report in seconds."
findings.after: Name the report and the mechanism, e.g. 'Pick the dates; the movement book and medicine record come out in the standard layout' ([DATA NEEDED: confirm formats])
findings.why: Small puffery in an otherwise factual page.

strengths: Copy is in the farmer's vocabulary and concrete: '12 ewes to Top Field', 'Wormer, batch 4471, 8 lambs, 21 day withdrawal', 'Holding numbers saved', 'Stock left in the cabinet', 'Works without signal'. Do not dilute it.
Honest pricing and risk reversal: '£12 a month per farm. No card needed to start.', 'Cancel any month, keep your records', and an FAQ that answers real hesitations ('What if I stop paying?').
The medicine-record table is a telling product state that shows the inspection payoff directly.
Headlines have voice: 'Set up before tea.', 'Ready when they knock.'
not_investigated: image-only item: no DOM, no mechanical sweep; tells such as fonts, exact colours and radii judged by eye
Look family: cream ground and bold serif display touch warm-paper-serif, but the accent is farm green with a yellow action colour, no eyebrows or section numbering; not a cluster
Integrity of sample data ('Hill Farm', batch numbers) treated as illustrative product state, not as claims
